correctness.rationale: Sine law for consecutive origin-vertex triangles gives sin(alpha_i)=sin(alpha_(i-1)+Delta). The possible recurrences are rising R by Delta or reflection F: alpha_i=pi-Delta-alpha_(i-1). Strict polygon convexity gives an F transition only with alpha_(i-1)<pi/2; at global minimum the incoming transition must be F, and any later R would force indefinitely increasing R steps, contradiction. Hence alpha and radial coordinates have period two; odd n requires regularity. Even n=2h has a,b>0, side constraint ell^2=a^2+b^2-2cos(Delta)ab and strict-turn conditions a>cos(Delta)b, b>cos(Delta)a. Shoelace A=(n/2)ab sin(Delta), derivative in t=a/b has unique maximum t=1 and boundary infimum n ell^2/2 cot(Delta). Independent Cartesian edge/turn/area calculation checked representative orders n=3..12; all-n claim analytic.
